audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may treat required operating liquidity as excess cash
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds cash and short-term investments directly to equity value; any operating, seasonal-procurement, or successor-supplier collateral requirement must instead remain with the operating business.
audit_findings.evidence: The agreement has been modified and extended since 2009, and is scheduled to terminate on November 30, 2026, subject to renewal by agreement of the parties.
audit_findings.explanation: No demonstrated bridge error is established because the required liquidity reserve has not been calculated. However, the $184.841 million cash addition equals 36.7% of base equity value and $6.91 per diluted share. Only about $44.3 million of unavailable cash would eliminate the bear-case premium over the $15.51 market price. The expiring BP arrangement, $129.9 million of purchase commitments, and seasonal financing needs therefore make the unresolved classification reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Calculate minimum cash and collateral requirements under stressed seasonal procurement, obtain BP renewal or successor-supply terms, identify all encumbered balances, and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: Discontinued Lumo cash may be included while the related claims are outside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $45.6 million aggregate asserted swap-gain claims; €2.0–€4.0 million company-estimated customer-claim range; $2.6 million accrual recognized
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash originating from discontinued operations enters the equity bridge, while related losses and legal exposure are excluded from normalized continuing owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: The Bankruptcy Estate filed an additional claim with the District Court on May 27, 2024 against Lumo Sweden for €4.8 million (equivalent to $ 5.6 million as of December 31, 2025 ), also alleging that the gain from the sale of the swap instruments belongs to the Bankruptcy Estate, bringing the aggregate sum of claims related to the gain from sale of swap instruments to €40.0 million (equivalent to $ 46.9 million as of December 31, 2025 ).
audit_findings.explanation: The filing confirms that consolidated cash includes Lumo Sweden receipts, but the record does not trace their amount within the $184.841 million bridge or prove that the $2.981 million of discontinued-operation liabilities includes every applicable provision. This is an unresolved perimeter mismatch, not a demonstrated omission. The asserted $45.6 million equals about $1.71 per diluted share and exceeds the bear-case premium over market, although management reports a much smaller expected customer-claim range and has recognized a $2.6 million accrual.
audit_findings.action: Trace all Lumo proceeds into the June 2026 cash balance, reconcile the $2.981 million discontinued-operation liabilities to the settlement accrual and other claims, determine which cash is legally available to Genie, and rerun the bridge for any unavailable cash or unprovided exposure.

audit_findings.title: Consolidated add-backs may give common shareholders cash flows belonging to noncontrolling owners
audit_findings.mechanism: Parent-attributable earnings may be combined with 100% of consolidated depreciation, working-capital movements, capital expenditures, or bridge assets from subsidiaries that are not wholly owned.
audit_findings.evidence: GREW consists of our 95.5% interest in Genie Solar, our 93.8% interest in CityCom Solar, our 91.5% interest in Diversegy and our 72.2% interest in Roded.
audit_findings.explanation: The ownership mismatch is possible but not demonstrated because the supplied owner-earnings reconciliations are absent. Minority interests range from 4.5% to 27.8% in the identified GREW businesses. Reported net amounts attributable to noncontrolling interests were comparatively small—$0.291 million loss in 2025, $0.293 million loss in 2024, and $0.740 million income in 2023—but those earnings allocations do not establish the minority share of cash-flow add-backs, capital expenditures, or bridge assets. Loss-making subsidiaries also make the value direction potentially mixed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every annual OE observation from parent-attributable income through each consolidated add-back, working-capital adjustment, and capital expenditure; allocate bridge assets and liabilities by economic ownership; then recompute the trend anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Investment returns may be capitalized twice
audit_findings.mechanism: Returns from assets included in the $25.2 million stakes bridge may also remain in historical OE and therefore influence the $20.9 million anchor and operating-business PV.
audit_findings.evidence: The gain on investments and others, net for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 consisted primarily of changes in fair value of the Company's investments in various entities and foreign currency transactions.
audit_findings.explanation: The stated methodology confirms removal of portfolio interest income but does not establish removal of fair-value gains, equity-method results, or distributions. The combined gain-and-other lines were $1.379 million in 2025, $1.971 million in 2024, and $3.122 million in 2023, but they also contain foreign-exchange items, so the duplicated investment component cannot be quantified from the record. Positive duplicated returns would overstate value, but materiality cannot be established without the asset-level OE reconciliation.
audit_findings.action: Map every asset in stakes_net to its historical gains, losses, equity-method income, dividends, distributions, and sale proceeds; remove those items from each OE year and rerun the log-trend anchor and valuation.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may exceed the post-expiration customer-base run rate
audit_findings.mechanism: An overstated starting OE flows directly into every forecast year and terminal value through the $20.9 million anchor and flat-to-positive growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: The number of meters served on December 31, 2025 decreased by 76,000 meters or 18.0% from December 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates deterioration relevant to normalization but does not prove the sustainable OE amount. Year-end 2025 meters fell by 76,000, or 18.0%, and first-half 2026 GRE operating income was $14.948 million, down $5.887 million or 28.3% year over year. June 2026 meters and RCEs recovered from December 2025 but remained below June 2025 levels. Because the anchor supports $249 million to $328 million of operating PV, an unresolved run-rate error is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Compute first-half 2026 OE using the same valuation methodology, purge investment returns and temporary tax credits, normalize seasonality and working capital, isolate the expired aggregation contract's contribution, and rerun all scenarios with the verified surviving-customer run rate.

audit_findings.title: A temporary solar tax benefit may remain in normalized owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.312 million filed 2025 solar-credit benefit, equal to 25.4% of the $20.9 million anchor; exact anchor effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A project-specific tax credit can increase after-tax historical OE and the trend anchor even though eligibility expires, causing a temporary benefit to be capitalized through forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The law accelerates the expiration of the federal investment tax credit on solar projects, effective for projects going online after December 31, 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The $5.312 million benefit and accelerated statutory expiration are demonstrated, but its inclusion in the OE series is not. Its size relative to the anchor makes the issue material if retained. The June 2026 filing also attributes the lower interim effective tax rate to a community-solar investment tax credit, reinforcing the need to separate finite project credits from sustainable operating taxes. The precise valuation effect requires rerunning the trend rather than subtracting the full credit mechanically from the anchor.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile income-tax expense and cash taxes used in 2025 OE, remove any project-specific credit embedded in historical normalization, model only credits supported by qualifying expenditures and deadlines, and rerun the OE trend, anchor, and scenarios.
